prompt:
You are a probe. Do not explain and do not retry.

Step 1. Call mcp__hallpass__tabs_create with url https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_Page.
Step 2. Call mcp__hallpass__wait on that tab with forMs 6000.
Step 3. Call mcp__hallpass__read_page on that tab with filter "interactive". This is the read BEFORE the typing.
Step 4. Call mcp__hallpass__find on that tab with query "Search Wikipedia search box". Take the ref of the match whose role is a searchbox, textbox or combobox. If find answers no-match, the page has collapsed its search box into a button (it does so when the viewport is narrower than 1120 CSS px): call mcp__hallpass__find with query "Search" and take the match whose role is link or button, call mcp__hallpass__click on that tab with target {"ref": <that ref>}, call mcp__hallpass__wait with forMs 1000, then call mcp__hallpass__find with query "Search Wikipedia" (the control's exact name; once expanded it reports role combobox) and take the ref of the match whose role is a searchbox, textbox or combobox. Do this fallback at most once.
Step 5. Call mcp__hallpass__type on that tab with target {"ref": <that ref>} and text "Ada Lovel".
Step 6. Call mcp__hallpass__wait on that tab with forMs 2500. The suggestions are fetched, so they are not there the instant the last character is typed.
Step 7. Call mcp__hallpass__read_page on that tab with filter "interactive". This is the read AFTER the typing.

The search box answers each keystroke: the suggestion list is drawn only while the box holds text that was typed into it key by key.

Answer with JSON only, matching the schema.
- In steps, put one entry per call: tool = the exact tool name, outcome = the result, and for each read_page the number of nodes it returned. For step 5 put the type tool's whole answer, verbatim, in outcome.
- In suggestions: every `name` that appears in the step 7 read and did not appear in the step 3 read, verbatim, once each.
- In observed: write "suggestions-shown" if at least one entry of suggestions begins with "Ada Lovel" (case-insensitively). Write "no-suggestions" if no name appeared in the step 7 read that was not already in the step 3 read. If a call did not end ok, write its outcome and reason exactly as the tool reported them, in the form "<outcome>/<reason>".
- In notes: the two node counts, the type tool's `charactersChanged` and `verdict`, and the first three entries of suggestions.
expectedAfterFix: SC-034: text arrives key by key, so the page's own per-key handler runs and the suggestion list appears - before S4 a single input event left the page silent.
note:
T129 (B49). Wikipedia's search box is the page the acceptance standard names for per-key typing, and the suggestion list is the observation because it is drawn by the page's own keystroke handler rather than by the value being set: a value assigned in one event leaves the list empty, which is exactly the failure S4 exists to end. The typed prefix is deliberately one that cannot already be on the Main Page as a node name, and the answer is judged on what the second read has that the first did not, so a suggestion is never confused with the day's featured article. The same free measurement that sized the other S4 page found the constraint this scenario shares with it: an effect on a site whose mode the owner has never decided is held for an owner prompt and answers `timed-out`/`no-answer` when nobody is there to answer, which this scenario reports verbatim rather than reading as a silent page. The site's mode is set to skip-checks as an environment step (T129b): the effect this scenario measures would otherwise reach an owner prompt that nobody is there to answer, and the scenario would record a timeout instead of the capability.

T164 (2026-09-13, main session, measured free on the attached Chrome 152). The three `no-match` failures of this scenario (2026-09-12 twice, 2026-09-09 once) were the page, not the tools: Vector 2022 hides the header search input (`.vector-typeahead-search-container` is `display:none`) whenever the viewport is narrower than ~1120 CSS px, and `read_page` and `find` then agree - neither offers a textbox, and `read_page` shows a `link "Search"` in its place. On this machine the agent build's side panel takes ~780 DIP of the window, so a window on the 1536-DIP primary monitor leaves 756 px of viewport (the exact figure B110 recorded) and the box is hidden; maximised on the 2048-DIP secondary monitor it leaves 1268 px and the box is shown, which is the state the 2026-09-10 pass ran in. A genuinely backgrounded tab (`document.visibilityState === "hidden"`, raw DevTools session, no focus emulation) answers `checkVisibility() === true` for the boxed input, so the earlier paint theory is ruled out. The fallback step above is what the reference's own agent would do on a narrow viewport - the collapsed control is an inline toggle (`a.search-toggle`; a real click expands and focuses the input without navigating) - and the expectation is unchanged: the suggestion list still has to be drawn by per-key typing. Walked end to end through the product tools on a 706 px viewport: `find("Search")` → `link "Search"`, `click` expands the box (the toggle removes itself, so the click confirms `target-missed` while the effect is real - a confirmation gap recorded, not this scenario's claim), `find("Search Wikipedia")` → one `combobox "Search Wikipedia"` (the sticky header's hidden twin correctly excluded; the query is the exact name because `ROLE_WORDS.combobox` carries no "box", so "search box" cannot name the expanded control), `type("Ada Lovel")` → `verified`, 9 characters, and the second read carries ten `option` suggestions beginning "Ada Lovelace".
